channel.title: Cadence Evidence — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 56 sources.

item.title: Network-Based Brain Stimulation: Targeting the Frontoparietal Network for Cognitive Rehabilitation After Stroke Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 21 RCTs found that non-invasive brain stimulation (NIBS) targeting the frontoparietal network significantly improved executive function (Hedges' g = 0.48), working memory (g = 0.41), and attention (g = 0.38) in stroke survivors, with superior outcomes when combined with cognitive training.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparative Effects of Neurostimulation- and Technology-Augmented Robot-Assisted Training on Upper-Limb Motor Recovery After Stroke: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A network meta-analysis of 103 trials (5,251 participants) found that rTMS plus robot-assisted training (RAT) yielded the largest improvement in Fugl-Meyer Assessment for Upper Extremity (FMA-UE) (MD 9.56 points vs. usual care), followed by low-frequency electrical stimulation (LFES) plus RAT (MD 7.52 points), compared to RAT alone (MD 3.83 points) for post-stroke upper-limb recovery.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Altered Cognitive Control and Cortical Oscillatory Dynamics in Athletes With ACL Reconstruction During Decision-Making Under Uncertainty.
item.description: In a controlled laboratory study of 90 open-skill athletes (45 non-ACLR, 45 ACLR), athletes with ACL reconstruction (ACLR) showed slower response times and lower accuracy (d = 0.75-1.09), alongside persistent alterations in cortical oscillatory mechanisms (attenuated prestimulus theta, elevated target phase theta, reduced beta/alpha suppression), reflecting impaired cognitive control, motor preparation, and attentional allocation during decision-making under uncertainty.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Interval Between Injury and Surgery Influences Knee Biomechanics During Walking in Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstructed Patients: A Systematic Review with Meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 16 studies found that delayed ACL reconstruction (≥12 months) is associated with persistent sagittal plane deficits in walking biomechanics, while early surgery (<6 months) correlates with fewer long-term sagittal-plane deficits but may have temporary frontal-plane asymmetries.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Efficacy of Manual Physiotherapy Techniques for Improving Cervical Range of Motion in Infants With Congenital Muscular Torticollis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of five RCTs (n=143 infants) found manual physiotherapy techniques significantly improved cervical ROM in infants with congenital muscular torticollis (Cohen's d = 0.90, 95% CI: 0.54 to 1.27, p < 0.001), indicating a large overall effect with low heterogeneity.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Diagnosis, Rehabilitation, and Return to Sport after Athletic Hamstring Injury: An ICCUS Society Consensus Statement.
item.description: An ICCUS Society expert consensus statement, developed via a modified Delphi process with 17 clinicians, achieved over 80% agreement on 54 statements concerning athletic hamstring injury management, emphasizing standardized classification, individualized criterion-based rehabilitation, progressive loading, and multi-faceted return-to-sport criteria.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Gait variability as a predictor of fall risk in patients with stroke: A 6-month prospective cohort study with survival analysis.
item.description: In a 6-month prospective cohort study of 112 stroke patients, stride time variability (STV) at discharge, with an optimal cutoff of 3.40% (AUC 0.756, sensitivity 88.2%, specificity 53.8%), was identified as the sole independent predictor of post-discharge falls, outperforming conventional measures.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Neurocognitive Factors in ACL Injury: The Missing Piece in Rehabilitation and Prevention? A Scoping Review.
item.description: A scoping review of 42 studies identified dual-task interference, visual attention, and reaction time as the most investigated neurocognitive domains in ACL injury. Neurocognitive training shows potential for improving visuomotor efficiency and return-to-sport readiness, suggesting these factors are a missing component in current ACL rehabilitation and prevention frameworks.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparative Efficacy of Low-Level Laser Therapy in Patients With Carpal Tunnel Syndrome: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
item.description: An updated systematic review and meta-analysis of 16 RCTs found low-level laser therapy (LLLT) significantly reduced pain (Hedges' g=-1.524, P <0.001) and improved grip strength (Hedges' g=0.391, P=0.002) in carpal tunnel syndrome. Pulsed mode was superior for analgesia, while continuous mode better supported grip strength.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of chair-based exercise training on pulmonary function, exercise capacity, and quality of life in patients with acute exacerbation of COPD: A randomised controlled trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial of 30 AECOPD patients found that chair-based exercise training significantly improved functional exercise capacity (79.7m vs 28.8m in 6MWT), dyspnoea, and quality of life compared to breathing exercises alone.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Five Days of Acute Intermittent Hypoxia Is Safe and Improves Somatic Motor Function in Persons with Multiple Sclerosis
item.description: A randomized, double-masked, placebo-controlled crossover trial in ambulatory MS patients found daily acute intermittent hypoxia (AIH) was safe and significantly improved ankle plantarflexion torque (17.5% post-intervention, 29.2% at follow-up) and 6-Minute Walk Test distance (β=10.14 m, p=0.039) compared to sham.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: Effectiveness of wearable and non-wearable biofeedback on knee biomechanics during functional tasks in anterior cruciate ligament injury prevention and rehabilitation: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 24 studies found that biofeedback significantly reduced peak knee abduction angle (Hedges’ g = 0.52, 95% CI 0.06 to 0.98, p = 0.03) in ACL injury prevention, but no significant effects for other knee biomechanics, with low to very low certainty of evidence.
item.author: BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil

item.title: Comparative diagnostic utility of SPECT-CT versus MRI and CT in chronic low back pain.
item.description: In a retrospective cohort of 122 patients with chronic low back pain, SPECT-CT positivity was moderately and independently associated with Modic changes, advanced Pfirrmann grade, and vacuum disc/facet phenomena on MRI/CT, but findings were frequently discordant, suggesting SPECT-CT may complement other imaging.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Gamified Versus Traditional Balance Training: Effects on Balance and Motivation in Collegiate Student-Athletes.
item.description: A quasi-experimental controlled trial of 30 collegiate athletes found that both gamified (Wii Fit) and traditional (wobble board) balance training similarly improved mSEBT composite scores (gamified: +21.6 ± 11.9 cm; traditional: +18.5 ± 14.6 cm) compared to control. However, the gamified group reported significantly higher intrinsic motivation (IMI interest/enjoyment: 5.0 ± 1.2 vs. 3.2 ± 1.3, p < 0.01).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Adherence System Usability Patient Experience and Psychosocial Impact in Robot Assisted Gait Neurorehabilitation A Cross Sectional Study.
item.description: A single-center observational study of 250 adults in robot-assisted gait neurorehabilitation found that greater attendance, System Usability Scale (SUS) scores (72.79 ± 12.06), and Neurorehabilitation Experience Questionnaire (NREQ) scores (27.84 ± 4.92) were associated with more favorable Psychosocial Impact of Assistive Devices Scale (PIADS) scores (1.67 ± 0.74), even after adjusting for diagnosis (all p < 0.001).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Physical and psychosocial outcomes in children with limb loss 2-years after the 2023 Kahramanmaras-Türkiye earthquakes
item.description: A retrospective analysis of children (mean 13.7 years) with earthquake-related limb loss 2.3 years post-amputation showed favorable child-reported PedsQL scores (median 72.3/100.0) for physical, social, and school domains, but lower emotional functioning (60.0/100.0), indicating the importance of long-term mental health support.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: Aqua Steps: A Feasibility Study of a new Aquatic Exercise Therapy Intervention for Falls Prevention in Older Adults.
item.description: A feasibility study of a new aquatic exercise intervention (Aqua Steps) with 101 older adults at high falls risk found high feasibility and acceptability. It reduced falls by 38%, fallers by 36%, and frequent fallers by 58%, with significant improvements in functional (22%-70%) and strength (10%-80%) tests.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Injury risk and physical therapy utilization following knee surgery in U.S. Army soldiers: a comparison of military and non-military treatment facilities.
item.description: A retrospective cohort study of 4924 U.S. Army soldiers found that those undergoing knee surgery at non-military treatment facilities (32% of cohort) had higher subsequent injury rates (79% vs. 73%) and longer physical therapy duration (8.3 vs. 7.1 weeks; p = 0.038) compared to those treated at military facilities.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effectiveness of a Structured Post-Platelet Rich Plasma Rehabilitation Approach on Pain and Function in Subacromial Pain Syndrome: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (n=54) for subacromial pain syndrome found that adding a structured post-PRP rehabilitation approach to conventional physiotherapy significantly improved pain (VAS: 2.92 vs. 7.96; SF-MPQ: 10.07 vs. 19.37; p < 0.001), muscle strength, range of motion, and shoulder function compared to conventional physiotherapy alone.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparison of robot-assisted gait training and visual feedback balance training on balance and gait outcomes in patients with stroke: a randomized controlled trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (n=50) in stroke patients found that visual feedback balance training (ProKin-252) led to a statistically greater improvement in Berg Balance Scale (adjusted difference of 1.43 points, 95% CI, 0.37-2.49; p = .009) and fear of falling compared to robot-assisted gait training (RoboGait), with both showing improvements in functional mobility and gait speed.
item.author: PubMed
